monthly_review.summary: You've increased intensity and efficiency this month while slightly reducing volume; pace has improved significantly despite lower total km.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved by +0.34 m/sec per bpm — the largest gain among all metrics — indicating better oxygen utilization at given heart rates.

goal_tracker.message: You need 12.6 more km across 3 sessions in the remaining 14 days to match last month’s volume — e.g., three 4.2 km runs at your current avg pace of 496 sec/km (8:16 min/km).

insights.title: Efficiency rising with intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency increased from 13.28 to 13.62 m/sec per bpm despite higher average HR (+7 bpm) and faster pace (−38 sec/km), suggesting improved cardiovascular economy.

insights.title: Zone 4 dominance this month
insights.body: Zone 4 effort rose from 12% (Mar) to 24% (Apr), while Zone 2 dropped from 47% to 30% — indicating a sharp shift toward threshold work and away from foundational aerobic base building.

insights.title: Cadence stable but stride length variable
insights.body: Cadence held steady at 150 spm, yet stride length varied widely across recent runs (70.96–90.77 cm), correlating with pace and HR — longest stride occurred at highest HR (163 bpm, 90.77 cm on 4/12), suggesting form compromise under fatigue.

insights.title: High-intensity density without recovery buffer
insights.body: Aerobic TE jumped from 3.0 to 3.5 this month, yet only 11% of April time was spent in Z1 (recovery zone) vs 4% in March — insufficient low-HR recovery volume to offset increased Z4/Z5 load (33% combined in Apr vs 13% in Mar).

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a 5 km Zone 2 session at ≤135 bpm (based on your avg HR of 142 in March and current Z2 upper limit likely ~138–140 bpm), aiming for cadence ≥152 spm and vertical oscillation ≤8.0 cm.
recommendations.reason: To rebuild aerobic base and increase Z1/Z2 time (currently only 11% this month), counterbalancing recent Z4/Z5 overload and supporting efficiency gains.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 km progressive run starting at 520 sec/km (8:40 min/km) and increasing pace by 10 sec/km every km — target HR staying ≤152 bpm through first 2 km, then allow natural rise in final km.
recommendations.reason: Improves pace adaptability while constraining HR drift — addresses your recent 7.42 min/km (445 sec/km) best pace occurring at 163 bpm (risk of unsustainable effort).

recommendations.action: Add a post-run mobility drill: 3 × 60 sec single-leg glute bridge (each leg) immediately after your next two runs, focusing on ground contact time <305 ms (your current avg is 307 ms, with range 301–311 ms).
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time is trending upward (301→311 ms across recent runs); targeted strength can improve stiffness and elastic return to support efficiency and reduce oscillation.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish Zone 1–2 as the physiological and neuromuscular foundation — prioritizing HR control, efficiency consistency, and recovery capacity before adding further intensity.
suggested_sessions: 3 km progressive pace run with HR ceiling
